title: Meet M2 Lab: who agreed to Friday?
hooks: This reply looks ready. But who agreed to Friday?
Before AI drafts anything, decide where it must stop.
The human check should be part of the process, not an afterthought.
full_spoken_english: This reply looks ready. But who agreed to Friday? Imagine a customer asks when an order will arrive. The note says the team is checking. The draft says Friday. At M2 Lab, we look for moments like this before connecting AI to everyday work. Draw a line between preparing a reply and making a promise. AI can work from approved facts; missing facts need a person. In this example, replace the invented date with a question for the order owner. Keep the customer's original message beside it. The useful output is an editable draft with the gap visible. Sending stays a separate decision. Take one message your team repeats. Underline every promise in the reply. Can you point to the fact and the person behind each one?
cta: Take one message your team repeats. Underline every promise in the reply. Can you point to the fact and the person behind each one?

fixture.input: Customer: When will my order arrive? Internal note: team checking; date unknown.
fixture.designed_output: Draft held for order owner: Please confirm the delivery date before replying.

audio_plan: Natural recorded voice; no imitation. Quiet room; optional subtle licensed music only after voice intelligibility check. No sound needed to understand proof panels.
caption_plan: Editable sentence captions, maximum two short lines; keep proof labels clear. Captions paraphrase nothing that changes a fact. Final platform safe-zone check after edit.
